beats.text: In 1909, this man stood near the top of the world, and history almost forgot him.

overlays.hook: In 1909, he stood near the *top of the world.*

beats.text: Born in Maryland in 1866, he went to sea as a cabin boy.
The ship's captain taught him to read and write.

visual.title: At sea
visual.sub: the captain taught him to read and write

beats.text: In 1887, working in a store in Washington, he met the explorer Robert Peary.
Peary hired him. Together they made seven expeditions to the Arctic.
Henson learned the Inuit language and became an expert dog-sled driver.
On April 6, 1909, Peary's team said they had reached the North Pole.

visual.caption: The sledge party with flags, April 1909

beats.text: Henson was there. Whether they reached the exact Pole is still debated.

visual.caption: Measurements of the sledge party, 1909 (National Archives)

beats.text: But Peary got the fame. Henson spent decades as a clerk in New York.
Recognition came slowly. In 1937, the Explorers Club finally made him a member.
In 1988, he was reburied at Arlington National Cemetery, near Peary.
He went to the end of the earth. It took the world almost eighty years to catch up.

visual.caption: Henson in 1953, holding his famous Arctic portrait

facts.claim: Born in Maryland, 1866; cabin boy at sea as a boy.
facts.note: Birth day differs (Aug 6 NG, Aug 8 BOW); script gives the year only. Age 12 (BOW, BP) or 13 (NG); script says 'as a cabin boy'.

facts.claim: The ship's captain taught him to read and write.
Met Peary in Washington, 1887, while working in a store (hat shop / clothing store).
Spoke the Inuit language; expert dog-sled driver.
On 6 April 1909 Peary's party claimed the North Pole; Henson was with him.
Whether they reached the exact Pole is disputed.
facts.note: BP: later research shows they did not reach it; NG: 1988 article 'Did He Reach the Pole?'. Script calls it 'still debated'.

facts.claim: Peary got the fame; Henson worked for decades as a clerk at the New York Customs House.

facts.note: BOW: 'belatedly admitted'; DART and CSMD give 1937 (first African American life member).

facts.claim: Reinterred at Arlington National Cemetery in 1988, near Peary.
